newsitem.title: USA: Florida judge moves forward on tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Florida judge moves forward on tobacco case.

text.p: Florida officials suing tobacco companies for nearly $1 billion need not supply the names of 860,000 Medicaid patients who have been treated for smoking-related illnesses, a state judge ordered on Friday.

Circuit Judge Harold Cohen, who is presiding over a civil lawsuit filed by the state against major cigarette makers in West Palm Beach, accepted as evidence the state's list of Medicaid patients identified only by identification number.
By doing so, Cohen denied a tobacco industry request that each name be provided to the defense team.
Tobacco representatives could not immediately be reached for comment.
Florida is suing the tobacco industry under a 1994 state law that allows the state to use market share data to apportion liability among individual companies.

Cohen, who in September ordered the state to turn over a list of recipients of Medicaid, also indicated that tobacco companies would not be allowed to depose thousands of patients as part of their defense, a move that could have postponed a trial indefinitely.
Cohen's ruling comes after the Florida Supreme Court struck portions of the law earlier this year. The high court, however, upheld the state's ability to use market share data to affix liability.

"The court will not become frozen in a snail's pace search for the truth," Cohen said in a four-page opinion. "I do not believe the Florida Supreme Court ... intended for the trial court to get bogged down in an endless stream of depositions and other pretrial discovery mechanisms not particularly suited to address the market share concept."

State officials hailed Cohen's ruling, saying it will bar tobacco defendants from postponing the trial by deposing all victims. Earlier in the week, the state delivered 44 boxes containing the list of Medicaid patients and payments made to providers.

"Judge Cohen's ruling means our case to protect our taxpayers and children from falling victim to 'Big Tobacco' won't drown in a sea of depositions and other legal maneuvers," Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles said Friday afternoon.
The case is scheduled to go to trial August 4, 1997.
